output.answer: The closest before-air runs still recorded flames, while at the after air the one run at that air recorded no ignition; this is evidence that lower oxygen can hinder burning, not proof it will put out this cabin fire [bass-asrun-55] [bass-ii-o12]. Lowering oxygen is not a reliable immediate fire response: the closest tests used different fuels, and the after-air test did not test an already-burning fabric fire.
output.whatChanges: No run sits at the before air; the closest result runs were 8.3–8.4 oxygen percentage points away and recorded flames, including a SIBAL run whose notes say the flame got smaller at maximum flow but did not blow out [bass-asrun-55] [bass-asrun-60]. At the after air, one run sits at that air and recorded no ignition; its outcome is based on investigator notes, and the closest identified run was 1.6 oxygen points away at the same pressure and also recorded no ignition [bass-ii-o12]. Nearby runs at 2.8–3.3 oxygen points above the after air recorded extinguishing or blowoff, but these were different fuels and do not establish what would happen to this fabric fire [bass-ii-o4] [bass-ii-b14] [bass-ii-o9] [bass-ii-o19].
output.whatYouWouldSee: With less oxygen, a flame is generally weaker and may look smaller, dimmer, bluer, less sooty, and spread more slowly; the provided runs do not directly compare the same fabric fire at both airs. Notes from other fuels describe sooty and blue flames [bass-asrun-89-row102] [bass-asrun-102], so they do not establish the appearance of this fire.
output.crew: The provided crew estimate changes from 4.56 psi oxygen partial pressure, equivalent to 0 m altitude and “Fine to breathe,” before, to 1.76 psi, equivalent to 4500 m and “Hypoxia likely,” after. The lower-oxygen air therefore presents a serious breathing concern for the crew.
output.instead: Use the cabin’s fire-response procedures rather than relying on lowering oxygen; microgravity ventilation feeds flames, and BASS runs record flames going out when airflow was reduced or turned off [bass-asrun-89-row102] [bass-asrun-90-row100]. Those airflow results are from other fuels, so the test that would settle this comparison is a burning fabric test at the after air with airflow controlled and recorded.
